solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A name's changed after run-of-the-mill rating

indicators.note: after places the rearranged piece behind the adjective in the answer

parts.note: run-of-the-mill means ordinary, nothing special

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of these words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor's name gets altered once he is assigned a humble naval grade.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a naval sailor, not a score; 'changed' signals the anagram and 'after' places it second.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a rating is a sailor below officer rank, and this is the lowest such grade.

clue.text: I provide a remedy which allows smooth flow

definitions.meaning: one who puts things right, a corrector of faults, could say this of themselves
an electrical device turning alternating current into steady direct current

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets things right is a rectifier, and so is the electronic component that makes current flow one way.

clue.text: Out of place in English exercises

parts.note: taken as written
PT, physical training, means exercises

explanation.surface: Something looks wrong in an English lesson's workbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or inappropriate, so a remark out of place is inept.

clue.text: Argonauts travelling about in bark

indicators.note: travelling about suggests the letters wander around into a new order

explanation.surface: Jason's heroic crew roam around aboard their sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like a ship (barque) in the Argonauts' story but is tree bark, used for the bitters.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is a South American tree bark, used to flavour the famous aromatic bitters.

clue.text: Remain up around end of audience with poet

indicators.note: around means the reversed word wraps round the next piece
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to remain is to stay

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of audience

explanation.surface: A poet is told to stay on stage after the audience has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns STAY into YATS, which goes 'around' E, the last letter of 'audience'.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate, an example of the category.

clue.text: Snaps World Fair, eg, with certain celebs finally

parts.note: a world fair is an example of an expo, a big exhibition
certain means sure

indicators.note: finally takes just the last letter of celebs

explanation.surface: Photographs taken at an international fair, with some famous guests at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic snaps are exposures, each frame of film exposed to light.

clue.text: We hear a mass of confused info for a source of food

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a maze is a bewildering tangle, a mass of confusion

explanation.surface: We are told a jumble of muddled facts leads to something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is a cereal crop and a staple food around the world.

clue.text: Female lingerie near gent's cravat?

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
a tie is a man's neckwear, of which the cravat is a kind; the question mark flags the loose fit

explanation.surface: A woman's underwear lies next to a man's neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress for women is nightwear, the sort of garment sold as lingerie.

clue.text: Thesis includes beginning of reinvestigation for Capricorn, say

indicators.note: includes means the first word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a thesis is a proposition or subject, a topic

indicators.note: beginning of takes only the first letter of reinvestigation

explanation.surface: An academic paper begins a fresh study of the goat sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Capricorn is one of the two lines of latitude bounding the tropics, an example.

clue.text: Check out playground next to church

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British playground or park
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Have a look at the play area beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, means to scout or survey a place, as a verb.

clue.text: Glaring slips about very soft wrestling

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
slips suggests the letters slide out of place into a new order

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Glaring errors are made around a gentle bout of wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' is the anagram signal, not errors, and 'about' wraps the musical marking inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling is close wrestling, struggling hand to hand with an opponent.

clue.text: Place this surprisingly around new bases

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
surprisingly suggests the word this turns up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Putting this down unexpectedly near some fresh foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles only 'this'; 'Place' gives its street-sign abbreviation, and 'around' wraps the new letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plinths are the flat slabs on which statues or columns stand, bases in the plural.

clue.text: Southern American loudly kissed one on bail, perhaps

indicators.note: loudly signals that the word is spelt as it is heard

parts.note: pecked means gave a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A southern American kissed someone out on bail, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' turns PECKED into its sound, PECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect, someone accused of a crime, may be released on bail before trial: an example.

clue.text: Gaffer and I must get into cook

indicators.note: must get into means the single letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: The boss and I need to get the cook involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman, and a chief is the person in charge.

clue.text: Fine's just horrible

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
just means fair or rightful

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a penalty is simply dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful means dreadful or shocking, a synonym for awful.

clue.text: Guarantee to pass on the wrong side?

definitions.meaning: to guarantee or pledge, to promise to do something

definitions.text: to pass on the wrong side?
definitions.meaning: a jokey verb for passing a car on the inside, the reverse of overtaking

explanation.definitionFit: To pledge is to undertake, and British drivers call illegal passing on the inside lane undertaking.

clue.text: What receives a clump? Husband's drier

parts.note: a satellite dish receives signals
a clot is a clump, as of blood
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Who takes a blow? The husband who does the drying-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clump' here is a lump, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel for drying washed crockery is a drier in that sense, a cloth for dishes.

clue.text: Pickle in a pitta's for starters

indicators.note: a pickle is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: There is a pickle tucked into the pitta bread as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like food, but here it means a mess, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Leading dignitaries in a RC island mass

indicators.note: mass suggests the letters are gathered into a jumbled heap

explanation.surface: Senior clergymen gather on a Catholic island to celebrate Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like the church service, but it signals a jumble of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals are senior princes of the Roman Catholic Church, high-ranking churchmen.

clue.text: Cold cream I replaced in china bowl, say

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Cold cream was swapped into a porcelain dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' shuffles only 'cream I'; the abbreviation for cold stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A china bowl is an example of a piece of pottery or fired clay, used as a noun.

clue.text: Posed with your woodland god

parts.note: a model posed or sat for an artist
YR is a written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: Someone modelled alongside you for a portrait of a forest deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a half-goat spirit of the woods in Greek myth.

clue.text: Concerned with black French painter

parts.note: RE means concerning, as in letter headings
noir is the French word for black

explanation.surface: Interested in dark tones, a French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was the French Impressionist artist, an example of the type.

clue.text: This garden plant's fruit proved trendy

parts.note: dough that has proved has risen, so rose
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Fruit from the garden turned out to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proved' means rose, as bread dough does.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fruit left on a rose bush after flowering is the hip.

clue.text: This racing driver should make you want to go quickly

definitions.meaning: Ayrton ... was a Brazilian Formula One champion

definitions.text: should make you want to go quickly
definitions.meaning: the laxative made from cassia plants

explanation.definitionFit: Ayrton Senna was a Formula One great, and senna pods are a well-known laxative.

clue.text: Dad's first pair of teeth finding gum

parts.note: pa is dad, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: first pair of takes the opening two letters of teeth

explanation.surface: Father's front teeth turn up stuck in chewing gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste and gum are both adhesives used for sticking paper.

clue.text: Check concerning mountaineer's safety aid

parts.note: to cramp is to restrict or check
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Inspecting a climber's protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked frame strapped to a boot for grip on ice, a climbing aid.

clue.text: Raise claim with a Greek story-teller

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the letters are lifted to read upward, backwards

parts.note: to pose a claim, so pose means put forward

explanation.surface: Lodge a demand alongside an ancient teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns POSE A upward into AESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the Greek author credited with a famous collection of fables.

clue.text: A written declaration from chap with independent party, Oscar

parts.note: a chap is a man
a fest is a festive party
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An independent candidate named Oscar publishes his election platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of aims, typically by a party or group.

clue.text: Curt greeting follows suspect food

indicators.note: follows places the greeting after the slang word

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicious or suspect
hi is a brief hello

explanation.surface: A brusque hello comes after some dubious food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish, an example of food.

clue.text: Fool bloke with line in The Tramp, commonly

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool
a chap is a bloke

explanation.surface: A silly man walks in a line with a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent-film star was widely known by his screen character, the Little Tramp.
